_meta.indication: Central alpha-2 adrenergic agonist indicated for mitigation of opioid withdrawal symptoms to facilitate abrupt opioid discontinuation in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Inpatient, randomized, multi-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study of lofexidine 3.2 mg/day (0.8 mg QID) vs placebo for 5 days.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults dependent on short-acting opioids undergoing opioid withdrawal management.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Prespecified primary endpoints: SOWS-Gossop score on Day 3 and time-to-dropout.
pivotal_trials.result: Day 3 SOWS-Gossop LS mean difference -2.24 (95% CI -3.88, -0.60; p=0.009) favoring lofexidine. Completion rate through treatment phase significantly higher (p=0.009) in lofexidine (49%) vs placebo (33%); retention log-rank p=0.0040.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled for 7 days (LFX 2.4 mg/day, LFX 3.2 mg/day, or placebo QID) followed by open-label, variable-dose treatment for up to 7 additional days.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Prespecified primary endpoint: SOWS-Gossop scores from Days 1 to 7; secondary endpoint completion status on Day 7.
pivotal_trials.n: 602 subjects (Placebo N=151, LFX 2.4 mg N=229, LFX 3.2 mg N=222)
pivotal_trials.result: SOWS-Gossop Days 1-7 log-scale LS mean difference significant vs placebo for both doses (LFX 2.4: -0.21, 95% CI -0.37, -0.04, p=0.017; LFX 3.2: -0.26, 95% CI -0.44, -0.09, p=0.003); no significant difference between the two doses. Completion at Day 7 ~40% in lofexidine groups vs 28% placebo (p=0.007 LFX 2.4; p=0.019 LFX 3.2).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10% and notably more frequent than placebo) are orthostatic hypotension, bradycardia, hypotension, dizziness, somnolence, sedation, and dry mouth. In the label's two-dose study (assigned daily doses lofexidine 2.16 mg/day N=229, 2.88 mg/day N=222, vs placebo N=151), rates were: orthostatic hypotension 29/42/5%, bradycardia 24/32/5%, hypotension 30/30/1%, dizziness 19/23/3%. Serious risks include hypotension, bradycardia, syncope and QT prolongation.
target_moa: Lofexidine is a central alpha-2 adrenergic agonist with pharmacological properties similar to clonidine; it mitigates symptoms associated with opioid withdrawal.

rems.type: No risk evaluation and mitigation strategies are recommended for this product.

advisory_committee.vote: Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee met March 27, 2018; 11 of 12 members voted YES for approval.

basis.text: The Applicant requested Fast Track designation in October 2016, and the Division granted the request, designating the lofexidine program as a Fast Track development program for the facilitation of opioid discontinuation treatment in December 2016.

summary.text: US World Meds submitted NDA 209229 for lofexidine (LUCEMYRA), received September 26, 2017, reviewed as a Priority NDA; the Applicant had requested Fast Track designation in October 2016. A Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting was held March 27, 2018 (11 of 12 voted YES), and the application was approved first cycle for mitigation of opioid withdrawal symptoms to facilitate abrupt opioid discontinuation in adults.

citations.quote: US WorldMeds, LLC submitted NDA 209229 to support marketing approval of LUCEMYRA (lofexidine HCl), a central alpha-2 adrenergic agonist, for the mitigation of symptoms associated with opioid withdrawal and facilitation of completion of opioid discontinuation treatment. The Applicant requested Fast Track designation in October 2016 on the basis that lofexidine was being developed as a treatment for a serious aspect of a life-threatening condition and had the potential to address an unmet need.
A meeting of the Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee was held on March 27, 2018 to discuss this application. Eleven out of 12 members voted YES for approval of this product.
